themes_detail.label: Sudden Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 191 THIS WEEK—a 495% surge versus the 8-week baseline of 32.1 weekly complaints—signaling a rapid, widespread deterioration in road conditions across Sunnyside/Woodside that demands immediate investigation into root cause and scope.
evidence: 191 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 32.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (495% spike, z-score: 8.08)
Accompanying sidewalk condition spike: 21 complaints last week vs. 5.0 weekly average (320% increase, z-score: 4.72)
Combined street + sidewalk complaints represent largest sustained infrastructure spike in dataset
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Which streets are affected? Interview residents and document specific hazards (potholes, cracking, flooding).
DOT accountability: Why weren't these conditions caught earlier? Has street maintenance been deferred or redirected?

themes_detail.label: Tree Planting Demand Surge
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests jumped to 4 complaints THIS WEEK—a 3100% spike above the 0.1 weekly baseline—suggesting either a coordinated community push for greenery or sudden awareness of canopy gaps in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 4 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for 'new or expanded park or amenity' (documented annually)
Spike is recent and concentrated, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Community organizing: Is a local environmental or civic group mobilizing residents? Are they targeting specific neighborhoods or blocks lacking shade?
Parks equity: Which areas of CD 402 lack tree canopy? How does this compare to neighboring districts?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Infestation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 5 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO—a 3900% spike above the 0.1 weekly baseline—indicating a sudden wave of graffiti, advertisements, or signage defacement that may reflect organizational dumping or gang activity.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% spike, z-score: 14.74)
Spike is temporally isolated (peaked 3 weeks ago), suggesting event-driven cause rather than ongoing pattern
No corresponding Reddit or community board escalation visible
reporting_angles: Visual documentation: Map the locations and types of illegal postings. Are they political, commercial, or gang-related?
Sanitation response: How quickly is the city removing postings? Is there a backlog in this district?

themes_detail.label: Construction Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints jumped to 4 last week—a 3100% spike above the 0.1 weekly baseline—pointing to potential unsafe construction practices or site conditions in active building projects across the district.
evidence: 4 BEST/Site Safety complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Coincides with active DOB permit surge: 622 total filings in last 90 days, including 108 new buildings and 416 alterations
Multiple active ULURPs in pipeline (Hunters Point Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd rezoning) suggest continued development activity
reporting_angles: Site inspections: Partner with DOB to identify which projects triggered safety complaints. Are they repeat offenders?
Worker + community safety: Interview residents near construction sites and construction workers about conditions.

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise + Animal Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK (1100% above baseline), while unsanitary animal complaints on private property jumped to 4 last week (1500% spike), together suggesting elevated quality-of-life issues affecting public health and resident comfort.
evidence: Panhandling complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Unsanitary animal complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Both spikes are recent and converge on quality-of-life deterioration rather than single-issue crisis
reporting_angles: Street-level conditions: Are panhandling and animal complaints concentrated in specific neighborhoods or transit corridors?
Root causes: Are these increases tied to economic hardship, housing insecurity, or lack of animal control resources?
